text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High p99 tail latency detected for hosted streaming in eu-west2. Metric: streaming.tail.p99=820ms (SLO 300ms) — paging on-call

eve (oncall): seeing this on the dashboard, p95 around 220ms but p99 huge. streaming stalls reported by several customers.

maya (customer-ops): flagged a customer onboards ticket, user reports frequent stalls when streaming long completions.

alice (sre): reproducing on grafana: spikes correlate with increased cross-zone egress in eu-west2 AZ-B->AZ-C around 10:12UTC. Packet loss and TLS handshake retries visible.

sam (netinfra): I'm seeing NAT ephemeral port exhaustion signs on the hop to our egress gateway, conntrack high, retransmits rising.

eve (oncall): ok prioritize: 1) confirm customer impact 2) mitigate live 3) escalate to netinfra if needed.

maya (customer-ops): impact: 6 paying customers with streaming sessions active, 2 reported visible timeouts, others slower but not fully failing. CS notified.

oliver (eng): logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts from streaming workers to model pool nodes during high fanout. Example: `TLS handshake timeout after 10s` entries.

alice (sre): p99 tail spikes align with batching backlog and long socket stall timeouts in our streaming proxy. stack traces point to blocked send() on the egress path.

sam (netinfra): running quick checks: `ipvs` counters ok, but NAT table ephemeral ports in ephemeral range 32768-61000 are nearing capacity on some hosts. Might be a NAT path bottleneck to the internet egress.

eve (oncall): can we temporarily route traffic to a different egress path / region to break the spike? any quick reroute option?

sam (netinfra): yes, we can steer egress for a subset of pods to the alternate nat pool in az-a which has more ephemeral capacity. I can kick a route rule in 2-3 mins.

incident-bot: ACTION: paging sam (netinfra) — acknowledged.

sam (netinfra): started a partial egress steer: applying policy `egress.steer=eu-west2-az-a-nat` for streaming-proxy replicas id 12-20. Monitoring.

alice (sre): after steer, p99 drop from 820ms -> 420ms in 45s. p95 stable. Still above SLO but better.

eve (oncall): good. what's residual customer impact?

maya (customer-ops): customers report reduced stalls; one still seeing mid-stream disconnects. We're triaging with them, no escalations yet.

oliver (eng): investigating root cause: hypothesis is connection churn + NAT port limits causing handshake retries and queue backlog. Suggest increasing ephemeral port range and lowering connection churn via connection pooling.

sam (netinfra): agree. For immediate mitigation: 1) keep partial steer 2) bump NAT ephemeral allocation for affected NAT gateway (non-disruptive) 3) create connection draining rules to avoid bursts during rollout. I'll perform 2 now.

incident-bot: NOTE: scheduled change window outside business hours avoided, performing emergency change.

sam (netinfra): NAT ephemeral pool increased + ephemeral port reclaim tuned, test results show fewer TIME_WAIT sockets. p99 now 280ms for streaming tail.

eve (oncall): excellent, p99 under SLO. Re-run canary for streaming heavy traffic to validate.

alice (sre): running 30m canary with synthetic streams, monitoring streaming.tail.p99/p95, TLS handshake retries, and packet loss.

maya (customer-ops): I’ll update customer status: degraded -> partial mitigation, advise retry/backoff and we'll follow up.

oliver (eng): quick follow-up: pushing a config to reduce client-side fanout and enable keepalive reuse which should cut new TLS handshakes by ~40%. Plan PR ready.

eve (oncall): handoff: I'm on for 30 more minutes then handing to alice for nighttime watch. alice, you have action items: verify canary, confirm no regressions in other regions, and follow up with netinfra for a permanent fix.

alice (sre): ack. I'll take over at 21:00UTC and open a follow-up ticket with netinfra to investigate NAT scaling and consider alternate egress designs (egress pools per cluster, or proxy pooling).

sam (netinfra): will open infra ticket INFRA-4872 with traces and mitigation steps (ephemeral bump, steer policy). Also propose long-term: add horizontal NAT gateway capacity and per-AZ connection quotas.

eve (oncall): summary for post-incident: cause probable NAT ephemeral exhaustion + increased connection churn -> TLS handshake spike -> streaming proxy send stalls -> p99 tail latency spike. Immediate mitigations: steer traffic, increase ephemeral pool, enable keepalive tuning. Outcome: p99 restored < SLO, customers partially mitigated.

maya (customer-ops): I'll send a customer-facing note once alice confirms stability.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved for paging group: on-call acknowledged and mitigation implemented.

alice (sre): closing loop: will run a 6hr retention trace and add an alert for ephemeral port usage crossing 70% to avoid repeat. Also schedule a postmortem with netinfra and eng-runner teams tomorrow.

eve (oncall): thanks all. tagging follow ups: @sam (netinfra) INFRA-4872, @oliver (eng) keepalive PR, @alice (sre) postmortem + monitoring.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED: brief mitigation successful, follow-ups assigned.
